headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: AutoGen can execute code and write files while Prefect can also reach the network, creating default-path leakage and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and run tool calls; Prefect can consume workflow metadata and call APIs. If Prefect ingests AutoGen-produced files or logs as trusted inputs, prompt-like content can steer downstream automation. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Prefect reads AutoGen-generated files or logs as workflow inputs
IF AutoGen writes attacker-controlled content into a shared working directory
mitigations: Separate working directories for the two agents
Require explicit file provenance tags before Prefect parses outputs
Disable automatic ingestion of free-form text files
Review any shared queue or handoff format for instruction-like content

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and has broad network egress; Prefect touches workflow metadata and also has broad network egress. In a shared workspace, AutoGen can write sensitive artifacts that Prefect may upload or expose through API calls. This is a default-path leakage risk, though the exact shared storage is not documented.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or workspace
IF Prefect transmits files or metadata derived from AutoGen outputs to external services
mitigations: Use separate workspaces with OS permissions
Redact secrets before any handoff
Restrict Prefect to metadata-only inputs
Turn off automatic artifact upload where possible
Audit outbound destinations for both agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses; Prefect is an orchestration system that may also mutate shared workflow state. Even without explicit git access, overlapping writes to the same directory or state store can race and corrupt outputs. Because shared-state behavior is developer-defined, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or state backend
IF Prefect tasks and AutoGen subprocesses run concurrently without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Add file locks around shared state
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Disable shell execution for nonessential AutoGen tasks
requires-engineering: add transactional state management

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, files, and structured outputs that Prefect may treat as workflow inputs. If Prefect acts on those outputs without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into automated pipeline actions. Prefect is an orchestrator, so the downstream blast radius can exceed a single step, but the pair does not prove fully autonomous action by default.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes AutoGen outputs without validation
IF those outputs drive task parameters, API calls, or deployment steps
mitigations: Insert schema validation between agents
Require human approval for action-bearing outputs
Compare outputs against a second source before execution
Log and diff all handoff payloads
Limit Prefect to read-only dry runs

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and application data, while Prefect is documented here as touching workflow metadata. No explicit residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is shown, so compliance risk is limited to documented gaps rather than a clear violation. The other agent is not cited because no compliance-specific surface is exposed in its profile.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into AutoGen prompts or files
IF Prefect retention or logging policies differ from the operator's policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared prompts
Review retention settings before deployment
Mask secrets in workflow metadata
Document data-class boundaries for both agents
